turns.text: Welcome to the interview.
"Hi. Yeah, ready when you are."
What time did you go to bed last night?
"Around 9:30, like usual on early-shift weeks."
Thanks. Approximately how many hours did you sleep last night? Would you say you slept well? Why or why not?
"About seven hours — went down around 9:30, up at 4:45. Woke up briefly around 2 when the cat got into my room, but that's about it. I'd call it a good night, yeah, nothing to complain about."
Thanks for explaining that. What was the last activity you engaged in before going to bed? And why did you choose to do that activity?
"Just a short walk around the block, then some reading in bed. Nothing fancy — kind of the same wind-down every early-shift night."
Thanks. What factors have most affected your sleep quality over the past two weeks?

"Honestly, not much has changed — the shift rotation's been steady. Maybe the housemate's cat has been more of a nuisance lately, gets into my room a couple nights a week, but that's a minor thing. Nothing major's been throwing me off."

Is that pretty typical for you, or has something changed recently with your sleep or schedule?

And overall, are you happy with how you are sleeping these days? Why or why not?

"Pretty typical, yeah — nothing's shifted with the schedule. And I'd say I'm happy enough with my sleep, honestly. It's not glamorous, but it works — I get my seven hours most weeks and I know how to handle the rough patches when the rotation flips."
Thanks for sharing that. You mentioned reading in bed as part of your wind‑down — what kind of things do you usually read at night? Any particular book or type of book recently?
"Nothing fancy, honestly — mostly crime novels, cheap paperbacks. Been working through a Fred Vargas one this week, few pages at a time before my eyes give out."
That makes sense, thanks. You’ve probably heard the advice that adults should get 7–9 hours of sleep a night. Does that feel practical for you right now?

"Practical enough for me, most weeks — I land around seven on both the early and night shifts. It's the rotation weeks that eat into it a bit, but I've made my peace with that. I don't lose sleep over the number, if you'll pardon the pun."
Thanks, that’s clear. Many people check their mobile phones, tablets, or computers right before bed. Do you do this too? Why or why not?
"Not really — phone stays on the charger in the kitchen once I'm winding down. Old habit more than discipline, honestly, I just never got into scrolling before bed."
Got it, thanks. Do you regularly use social media at other times of day? If so, how do you typically use it?

Not really, no — I check Instagram maybe once or twice a day, usually on my lunch break at work or a bit in the evening. Mostly just scrolling, following a couple of welding and motorbike accounts, nothing I'd call heavy use.
Thanks, that’s helpful. Now a couple of quick questions about technology in general: Do you regularly use AI chatbots, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or similar apps?
"Not really, no. I've messed around with one out of curiosity, saw what the fuss was about, but it's not part of my routine. I'm more of a look-it-up-on-a-forum type when I need something specific."
Thanks, that’s clear. If you could improve one thing about your sleeping habits, what would it be?
"Honestly, probably just not having to reset my clock every third week. The sleep itself is fine — it's the switching that gets old."
Given your work, studies, or daily responsibilities, do you think that kind of change—avoiding the regular shift switching—would be doable for you? Why or why not?

"Honestly, no, not really — the maintenance windows only open up after midnight when they shut down track access, so somebody's got to be there and it rotates through the crew. I could ask to be taken off nights permanently, but then it just lands on someone else, and I'd rather take my third the same as everyone."
46, structural welder, born in Lyon, still living in Lyon — never moved away.

Thanks, that’s all the main questions I had.

Before we wrap up, is there anything else you’d like to add about your sleep or your routine that we haven’t talked about?
